correctness.rationale: For L=kt⊕V, [t,v]=Av, m≥2, a nonzero tensor map N=(at+u)⊗(bt*+ψ) has N²=0 exactly when ab+ψ(u)=0. Direct expansion of the original torsion identity on t∧V and ∧²V, with no assumption on characteristic, is equivalent to ψ(Au)ψ=ψ(u)(ψ∘A) and aψ∧(ψ∘A)=0. The three exhaustive eigen/non-eigen/augmentation cases follow, even when m=2, with non-eigen u-space zero. The q−1 tensor-rescaling quotient gives Z_A(q)=q^m−1+[q/(q−1)]{E(q^m−1)+(q^m−1−E)(q^(m−2)−1)} and defect q^(m−1)(q+1)(q^m−1−E). Non-scalar A has a non-eigen covector, producing a square-zero N that violates torsion, so scalar rigidity holds over any field. Independent direct basis-torsion enumeration over F3,m2 found Z=56 for diagonal(1,2), Z=8 for irreducible action, Z=104 for A=0; the general proof, not these finite examples, supports universality.
residual_risks: Finite checks do not validate all fields; arbitrary-field scalar rigidity rests on the linear algebra proof.
